'''Majid Momhed-Heravi''' (born 1952) is an Iranian chemist and [[Distinguished Professor]] of Chemistry at [[Alzahra University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Momhed Heravi elected as distinguished professor of Al-Zahra University |url=https://alzahra.ac.ir/fa/w/-9-15 |website=Alzahra University |language=fa-IR}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=An Interview with Heravi |url=http://www.sahand-chem.com/articles/923-%DA%AF%D9%81%D8%AA%DA%AF%D9%88-%D8%AF%DA%A9%D8%AA%D8%B1-%D9%85%D8%AC%DB%8C%D8%AF-%D9%87%D8%B1%D9%88%DB%8C-%D9%BE%DA%98%D9%88%D9%87%D8%B4%DA%AF%D8%B1-%D8%A8%D8%B1%D8%AA%D8%B1-%D8%B4%DB%8C%D9%85%DB%8C-%D8%AC%D9%87%D8%A7%D9%86 |website=www.sahand-chem.com}}</ref>

==Life==
Majid M. Heravi was born in 1952 in Mashhad, Iran. He received his B.Sc. degree from the [[National University of Iran]] in 1975 and his M.Sc. and Ph.D. degrees from the [[Salford University]] in 1977 and 1980. He completed his doctoral thesis under the supervision of Jim Clarck. He started his career as a research fellow in Daroupakhsh (a pharmaceutical company) in 1981 [[Tehran]], joined as an assistant professor at [[Ferdowsi University of Mashhad]] in 1983, and was promoted to associate professor in 1993, and became a full professor in 1997. In 1999, he moved to [[Alzahra University]] as a professor of chemistry, where he is still working. He has previously been a visiting professor at [[UC Riverside]] and [[Hamburg University]]. His research interests focus on [[Heterocyclic Chemistry]], Catalysis, Organic Methodology and Green Synthetic Organic Chemistry.<ref>{{cite web |title=Majid Momhed-Heravi|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-9259-0591 |website=ORCID}} {{CC-notice|cc=0}}</ref>
